arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Anders argued that due process analysis adequately addresses potential defense impairments at sentencing.
Mr. Schowengerdt argued that the clause's purpose is to protect presumptively innocent defendants from charge-related harms.
Mr. Rowley argued that the speedy trial clause applies through the culmination of a criminal prosecution in sentencing.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the scope of the Sixth Amendment. The core issue is whether the right to a speedy trial ends when a defendant is found guilty or continues through sentencing.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to recognize that the speedy trial right covers sentencing delays.
The state wants the Court to limit the speedy trial right to the trial phase only.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the right protects defendants from prolonged uncertainty until the case concludes with sentencing.
The state argues the right protects only presumptively innocent defendants from the harms of a pending charge.
